comparison: Perfect agreement on rootlet-membrane connections (C3, C51-C60). Both evaluations find the cryo-ET observations of flexible protrusions from cross-striations well-supported. Reviewers praised the 'exceptional' micrographs and 'excellent contrast,' while OpenEval noted 'strong visual and analytical evidence.'

Perfect agreement on three-band classification (C4-C6, C65-C75). Both evaluations affirm the identification of D1/D2/A bands as a key finding with 'unprecedented level of resolution.' Reviewers and OpenEval both note this advances beyond prior work that did not distinguish band types.

Strong agreement on D-band structural features (C76-C86). Both evaluations support the cryo-ET observations of D-band morphology and sub-fiber alignment. Peer review includes C7 (filament flexibility) while OpenEval addresses this separately. Both praise the state-of-the-art imaging and analysis.

Perfect agreement on A-band features (C87-C97). Both evaluations accept the structural observations and the interpretation that surface accumulations are purification artifacts. Reviewers affirmed the overall model without questioning the compositional speculation.

Strong agreement on filament flexibility and heterogeneity (C99-C105, C122). OpenEval includes C7 and C139 in this evaluation, while peer review focuses on C99-C105, C122. Both praise the cryo-ET and image analysis revealing the 'highly flexible network of filaments.'

Perfect agreement on subtomogram averaging results (C8, C106-C132). Both evaluations affirm the identification of twisted coiled-coil structures and commend the 'state-of-the-art' methodology and 'exceptional' quality. No concerns raised about the structural modeling or crystal structure fitting.

Significant disagreement on confidence level for the proposed structural model (C133-C150). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting key aspects remain speculative (parallel vs. antiparallel arrangement, intermediary proteins) and require validation. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, affirming a 'compelling molecular model' without challenging speculative elements. OpenEval excludes C139 and C141 that peer review includes.

Significant disagreement on D-band composition claims (C155-C166). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing the compositional assignment is speculative without direct localization data and noting contradictory AlphaFold predictions. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting CEP68/CCDC102B candidacy as reasonable interpretation within the overall model.

Significant disagreement on A-band membrane connection model (C167-C178). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the specific alignment of rootletin N-terminus and identity of membrane-linking proteins are inferred rather than directly demonstrated. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting the model without critique as part of the detailed organizational framework.

Both evaluations support background and context claims, but address different subsets. OpenEval R10 covers C1-C30 (biological context and prior literature). Peer R11 covers C1-C64 and C151-C154 (background, protein composition, methods, and novelty claims). Both affirm methodological rigor and appropriate citation of prior work.

Both evaluations support protein composition background (C31-C45). OpenEval addresses these separately from other background claims, while peer review groups all background, methods, and novelty claims together. Both affirm appropriate citation and context-setting.

Both evaluations support sample preparation methods (C46-C50, C61-C64). OpenEval addresses methods separately, while peer review groups them with background claims. Both affirm the methods are well-optimized and clearly described.

Both evaluations support rootlet flexibility claims (C179-C182). OpenEval addresses these separately from main findings, while peer review groups them with summary claims (C183-C184). Both accept the flexibility observations and functional speculation as reasonable.

Both evaluations support novelty claims relative to prior work (C151-C154). OpenEval addresses these separately, while peer review groups them with background and methods. Both affirm appropriate citation and accurate characterization of advances.

Both evaluations support the summary of main findings (C183-C184). OpenEval addresses these separately as a concise summary, while peer review groups them with flexibility claims (C179-C182). Both affirm the summary accurately reflects well-supported findings.
